Load AEME output to the aeme object

Source: R/load_output.R
load_output.Rd

Reads the output of models that have already been run and, by default, stores it in the output slot of the Aeme object. With return_type = "output" the output is returned instead and the Aeme object is left as it was, which is useful for looking at extra output (see extra_vars) without storing it alongside the output already on the object.

Usage

load_output(
  aeme,
  model,
  path = NULL,
  lake_dir = NULL,
  model_controls,
  parallel = FALSE,
  cl = NULL,
  ens_n = 1,
  keep_diag = TRUE,
  extra_vars = "none",
  sed_layers = NULL,
  zone_summary = FALSE,
  return_type = c("aeme", "output")
)

Arguments

aeme

Aeme object.

model

character vector; models to use. One or more of "dy_cd", "glm_aed", "gotm_wet", "simstrat_aed2". Defaults to all models if not found in aeme.

path

character; directory where input files are located. Defaults to the path stored in aeme, or the current working directory if not set.

lake_dir

Path to the lake AEME directory. If NULL, it is derived from aeme/path.

model_controls

data.frame; model configuration, typically loaded via get_model_controls().

parallel

logical; run models in parallel. Defaults to FALSE.

cl

an object of class "cluster".

ens_n

numeric; ensemble number to allocate to model output which is loaded. Defaults to 1. A run with ens_n = 1 clears any existing output; a run with another number adds (or replaces) that member and keeps the rest.

keep_diag

logical; keep the diag (diagnostic/scalar) and sediment sub-lists of each model's output (variables with dimensions other than time or depth x time, keyed by raw model names). Default TRUE, which keeps whatever was requested through extra_vars (nothing is requested by default, so by default there is nothing to keep). Set FALSE to drop the sub-lists even if they were requested.

extra_vars

character; for GLM-AED, which sediment, flux and diagnostic variables beyond the standard set to read from output.nc. Default "none": only the standard variables (vars_sim and the lake fluxes) are read, so nothing extra is loaded or stored unless asked for. Otherwise AEME names from glm_extra_vars (e.g. "SED_temp"), raw netCDF names, the keywords "sediment" / "diag" (every variable in that sub-list), or "all" for every variable in the file (this was the behaviour before extra output had to be requested). Unrequested variables are never read, which keeps loading fast and ensemble output small. See read_glm_output().

sed_layers

integer; GLM-AED sediment layers to keep for variables with a sediment-layer dimension (SED_temp). NULL keeps all. See read_glm_output().

zone_summary

logical; for GLM-AED, also add an area-weighted lake-wide series for each requested sediment-zone variable. See read_glm_output(). Default FALSE.

return_type

character; "aeme" (default) returns the Aeme object with the output stored in it. "output" returns the output without storing it: a list named by model, with one aeme_output (see is_aeme_output()) per model, read in the same way (simulation window, daily means, unit conversions) as the output that is stored. Because nothing is stored, ens_n is ignored. The result can be given to functions that take a model output directly, such as plot_model_output(), but not to those that need an Aeme object, such as get_var().

Value

With return_type = "aeme", the updated Aeme object with model output. With return_type = "output", a named list of aeme_output objects, one per model.
